currentContext.business: Sejal Glass Limited, founded in 1998, is an architectural glass processing company manufacturing toughened glass, laminated glass, insulated glass units and decorative/specialised glass solutions for residential and commercial buildings, public infrastructure, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, industrial facilities, data centres and high-security applications. It operates manufacturing facilities in Silvassa, Taloja and Erode (India) and Ras Al-Khaimah (UAE), serving both domestic and international markets including the GCC region; overall tempering capacity increased during FY2025-26 to 24.01 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum from 7.80 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum following the acquisition of Glasstech Industries' architectural glass manufacturing business.

currentContext.strengths: Access to European-standard glass processing technologies|Exclusive, royalty-free technology licensing agreement with Polymer Technology SRO (Spain) for fire-rated glass, seen as uncommon among domestic manufacturers|Multi-location manufacturing platform across India (Silvassa, Taloja, Erode) and UAE (Ras Al-Khaimah) providing geographic diversification and load-balancing/cross-utilisation of management resources|Established UAE subsidiary with strong market positioning across the GCC construction sector|Centralised procurement practices to manage raw-material cost fluctuations|Automation-led manufacturing with real-time production monitoring, quality analytics and predictive/preventive maintenance
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen position in value-added and speciality glass segments|Improve capacity utilisation across facilities, particularly the newly acquired Taloja and Erode units|Expand presence in both domestic and international markets to reduce geographic concentration risk and create a more balanced business|Continue investing in technology and automation (advanced manufacturing equipment, automation-led systems, intelligent monitoring)|Diversify product portfolio into specialised, high-value segments — fire-rated glass, railway-grade glass, bullet-resistant glass and digitally printed glass|Use centralised procurement practices to manage raw-material cost fluctuation|Pursue R&D focused on product innovation, process improvement, systems integration and sustainability|Build a unified organisational culture and leadership pipeline across manufacturing locations and international operations ("One Sejal" philosophy; Lakshya 2030 vision-alignment programme)
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26 Sejal Glass acquired and operationalised two manufacturing units of Glasstech Industries (India) Pvt Ltd at Taloja (Maharashtra) and Erode (Tamil Nadu), transforming the Company from a single-location to a multi-location manufacturing platform and taking overall tempering capacity from 7.80 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum to 24.01 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum. The Taloja facility's modern furnace, equipped with Fully Conventional Technology, opened up a new Digital Printing Glass segment and also strengthened capabilities in bullet-resistant glass and advanced façade solutions; as a recently integrated facility it is described as carrying substantial capacity headroom for future growth. The Silvassa facility remains the core domestic manufacturing pillar (toughened, laminated, insulated and decorative glass). Cross-facility capacity utilisation across the manufacturing ecosystem is described as reflecting a mix of mature facilities running at healthy utilisation and newly integrated facilities (Taloja) providing strategic headroom; the UAE subsidiary's own capacity utilisation improved to 67% in FY2025-26 from 53% in FY2024-25. Going forward, the Company intends to expand domestically via geographic expansion and infrastructure-led opportunities, leverage its UAE platform for the GCC, Africa and other export markets, and continue to evaluate disciplined inorganic growth along with selective brownfield and greenfield expansion aligned with market demand, technology access and return expectations.

risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and volatility in global economic conditions may impact infrastructure investments, construction activity and export demand across key markets, particularly in GCC countries; fluctuations in energy prices and logistics costs may also affect operational stability and project execution timelines.

Changes in government regulations, taxation policies, environmental norms, labour laws and trade-related regulations across domestic and international markets may affect operational efficiency and compliance requirements within the flat glass industry.

risks.risk: Raw material and energy cost risk
risks.note: Manufacturing operations remain exposed to fluctuations in prices and availability of key raw materials such as glass, interlayers, chemicals and related inputs; variability in fuel, power and logistics costs may also impact operating margins and overall cost competitiveness.

The value-added glass industry remains highly competitive with the presence of organised and regional players across architectural and processed glass segments; increasing competition and pricing pressure may impact market share and profitability.

Dependence on information technology systems across manufacturing, supply chain, finance and business operations exposes the Company to risks from system disruptions, cyber threats, data breaches and operational downtime.

The Company remains exposed to risks related to liquidity management, interest rate fluctuations, working capital requirements and changes in overall market conditions, which may impact financial performance and cash flows.

one-line thesis: Sejal Glass delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with 72% YoY revenue growth and 17.5% EBITDA margins, driven by UAE resilience and initial Glasstech integration. The core investment story pivots to FY27 where India operations (currently low utilization) must ramp to 50%+ to unlock consolidated 18% margin guidance, offsetting potential UAE volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 116.85cr (Q4, +72% YoY), INR 401.36cr (FY26, +64% YoY); EBITDA: INR 20.47cr (Q4, 17.5% margin vs 14.5% prior), INR 66.32cr (FY26, 16.5% margin vs 14.4% prior); PAT: INR 11.42cr (Q4, +200% YoY), INR 29.03cr (FY26, +160% YoY); Order Book: INR ~500cr equivalent (UAE portion AED 60mn); Net Debt: INR 138cr consolidated (INR 70cr promoter loans, INR 68cr bank term loans). One-offs: Glasstech integration costs suppressed India margins in FY26; no tax outgo expected for next 2 years due to carry-forwards.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 25% base case (up to 40% if UAE stabilizes) for FY27; Target Topline >INR 500cr. Margin: 17.5%-18% EBITDA for FY27. Order Inflow: UAE maintaining AED 10.2-10.5mn/month; India Q1 FY27 expecting 20% QoQ growth. Capex/Commissioning: UAE expansion machines delayed by geopolitics, now scheduled for installation in Q2/Q3 FY27.
order book & pipeline: Strong visibility in UAE with AED 60mn (~INR 135-140cr) order book; Q1 FY27 revenue visibility of AED 31mn, improving to AED 35mn in Q2. India order book growing via railway tenders (Vande Bharat) and commercial projects.
segment / subsidiary detail: UAE: Dominant revenue contributor (~60% of FY26), focused on high-margin IG and Laminated glass for facades. India: Transitioning from plain tempered (low margin) to IG/Laminated. Glasstech units (Taloja, Erode) reached EBITDA breakeven in March 2026; targeting 10%+ EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. Silvassa unit operating at 17-18% EBITDA.
growth verticals / optionality: New product lines (Fire-rated from Spain, Bullet-proof, Digital printed) launching Q3 FY26, targeting 5-7% revenue mix in FY26 and 15-20% in FY27. Railway segment entry (2-3% revenue contribution). Geographic diversification: Exports to Europe initiated from India; African market push from UAE.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw material (float glass) prices up 7-8% due to energy surcharges; company passing through 80-90% of cost increases. Consolidated gross margin ~33-34% (UAE mix superior to India). India gross margin expansion expected as mix shifts from 60% plain tempered to high-value IG/Laminated, potentially lifting gross margin to 39-40% long-term.
capex / expansion: UAE expansion capex delayed one quarter due to geopolitical situation; funding via mix of internal accruals and local debt. India capex focused on overhauling acquired Glasstech assets to meet utilization targets.
capital allocation: Debt reduction prioritized (repaid some promoter loans in Q4). Equity warrants (4 lakh) callable within 18 months, proceeds earmarked for potential second acquisition (currently under due diligence).
risks & watch-items: UAE geopolitical instability impacting real estate demand or supply chains; slower-than-expected capacity utilization ramp-up in India (Glasstech units); raw material price volatility if pass-through mechanisms fail; execution risk on new product launches.
management quality / tone: Highly optimistic and confident despite external headwinds; emphasizes 'genie in the bottle' regarding UAE resilience; transparent about integration teething issues in India; bullish on FY27 margin expansion to 18%.
non-obvious takeaways: India revenue degrowth on a proforma basis (including pre-acquisition Glasstech) due to 2-quarter consolidation/re-engineering period and cessation of low-margin trading activities. Zero tax liability expected for next 2 years enhances cash flow. Saint-Gobain collaboration provides 4-5% price advantage and preferential order confirmation, not just marketing support.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising energy costs and float glass prices squeezing fabricators without pricing power. | Sejal Glass Limited | beneficiary | High | Company explicitly stated ability to pass through 80-90% of raw material cost increases immediately due to make-to-order model and strong client relationships. |
| UAE real estate slowdown and geopolitical tension reducing demand for building materials. | Unorganized UAE Glass Fabricators | loser | Med | Sejal maintains AED 60mn order book and stable payments, suggesting market share consolidation towards organized players with strong balance sheets during turmoil. |
| Need for specialized high-safety glass (fire/bullet) in Indian infrastructure/railways. | Sejal Glass Limited | beneficiary | Med | First-mover advantage in India with new fire-rated tech from Spain and active bidding for Vande Bharat tenders, differentiating from commodity tempered glass competitors. |

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sejal Glass Limited, founded in 1998, is an architectural glass processing company manufacturing toughened glass, laminated glass, insulated glass units and decorative/specialised glass solutions for residential and commercial buildings, public infrastructure, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, industrial facilities, data centres and high-security applications. It operates manufacturing facilities in Silvassa, Taloja and Erode (India) and Ras Al-Khaimah (UAE), serving both domestic and international markets including the GCC region; overall tempering capacity increased during FY2025-26 to 24.01 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum from 7.80 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum following the acquisition of Glasstech Industries' architectural glass manufacturing business.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 25% base case (up to 40% if UAE stabilizes) for FY27; Target Topline >INR 500cr. Margin: 17.5%-18% EBITDA for FY27. Railway segment entry (2-3% revenue contribution). Geographic diversification: Exports to Europe initiated from India; African market push from UAE.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Residential and commercial real estate momentum, particularly premium housing, office spaces and data centres, continues to support demand
- Investments across airports, metro rail, healthcare and hospitality projects creating opportunities for architectural glass solutions
- Government focus on rail modernisation, including high-speed train programmes and rolling stock upgrades, creating growing demand for specialised glazing solutions
- Growing focus on energy efficiency and sustainable construction, reinforced by green building standards and energy performance codes, accelerating adoption of insulated and laminated glass solutions
- UAE/GCC construction activity supporting international operations, though geopolitical developments caused volatility in regional trade flows and some near-term supply-chain disruption
- Improved capacity utilisation at the UAE subsidiary (rising to 67% in FY2025-26 from 53% in FY2024-25) driving consolidated revenue and margin improvement
- Standalone EBITDA margin moderated due to under-utilisation of capacity at the newly acquired Taloja/Erode units, which were operational for only part of the year
- Newer product categories (fire-rated glass, railway-grade glass, bullet-resistant glass) expected to contribute more as recently integrated facilities ramp up utilisation
- Industry-wide competitive intensity from organised and unorganised players, raw-material cost volatility, and dependence on construction/real-estate cycles remain structural demand risks
- UAE operations remained steady through the year, supported by a healthy order book and strong payment discipline across the customer base

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Raw material (float glass) prices up 7-8% due to energy surcharges; company passing through 80-90% of cost increases. Consolidated gross margin ~33-34% (UAE mix superior to India). India gross margin expansion expected as mix shifts from 60% plain tempered to high-value IG/Laminated, potentially lifting gross margin to 39-40% long-term.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction prioritized (repaid some promoter loans in Q4). Equity warrants (4 lakh) callable within 18 months, proceeds earmarked for potential second acquisition (currently under due diligence).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY2025-26 Sejal Glass acquired and operationalised two manufacturing units of Glasstech Industries (India) Pvt Ltd at Taloja (Maharashtra) and Erode (Tamil Nadu), transforming the Company from a single-location to a multi-location manufacturing platform and taking overall tempering capacity from 7.80 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum to 24.01 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum. The Taloja facility's modern furnace, equipped with Fully Conventional Technology, opened up a new Digital Printing Glass segment and also strengthened capabilities in bullet-resistant glass and advanced façade solutions; as a recently integrated facility it is described as carrying substantial capacity headroom for future growth. The Silvassa facility remains the core domestic manufacturing pillar (toughened, laminated, insulated and decorative glass). Cross-facility capacity utilisation across the manufacturing ecosystem is described as reflecting a mix of mature facilities running at healthy utilisation and newly integrated facilities (Taloja) providing strategic headroom; the UAE subsidiary's own capacity utilisation improved to 67% in FY2025-26 from 53% in FY2024-25. Going forward, the Company intends to expand domestically via geographic expansion and infrastructure-led opportunities, leverage its UAE platform for the GCC, Africa and other export markets, and continue to evaluate disciplined inorganic growth along with selective brownfield and greenfield expansion aligned with market demand, technology access and return expectations.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly optimistic and confident despite external headwinds; emphasizes 'genie in the bottle' regarding UAE resilience; transparent about integration teething issues in India; bullish on FY27 margin expansion to 18%.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Access to European-standard glass processing technologies
- Exclusive, royalty-free technology licensing agreement with Polymer Technology SRO (Spain) for fire-rated glass, seen as uncommon among domestic manufacturers
- Multi-location manufacturing platform across India (Silvassa, Taloja, Erode) and UAE (Ras Al-Khaimah) providing geographic diversification and load-balancing/cross-utilisation of management resources
- Established UAE subsidiary with strong market positioning across the GCC construction sector
- Centralised procurement practices to manage raw-material cost fluctuations
- Automation-led manufacturing with real-time production monitoring, quality analytics and predictive/preventive maintenance

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: UAE geopolitical instability impacting real estate demand or supply chains; slower-than-expected capacity utilization ramp-up in India (Glasstech units); raw material price volatility if pass-through mechanisms fail; execution risk on new product launches.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: India revenue degrowth on a proforma basis (including pre-acquisition Glasstech) due to 2-quarter consolidation/re-engineering period and cessation of low-margin trading activities. Zero tax liability expected for next 2 years enhances cash flow. Saint-Gobain collaboration provides 4-5% price advantage and preferential order confirmation, not just marketing support.
